cases.bounds: The existing race/failure cases start with one published approval and two selectors. The retirement case has one request in one instance, one creation receipt, one selecting worker or claimed timer, one stop and a replacement admission boundary, or one admitted list/worker-permission query. Callback and storage completion may succeed or fail. Persisted cases project one task requiring both callbacks (sync or async, including the coding-tools caller) or one callback-free async task, one positive live deadline, one runtime restart, and one same-name worker re-registration. Callback completion and task deletion can succeed or fail. Task reads succeed in this projection.
limitations: Role authorization, option validation, multiple pending approvals, durable recovery of task rows and process restart are outside these projections.

Stopping an already-pending request retains its durable task row. Callback failure retains the row but removes its in-memory callback. Unavailable callbacks now fail closed. There is no durable callback retry or function reconstruction.
Retirement assumes admitted callbacks settle and do not await their own service unload or stop. Independent instances running concurrently and reentrant lifecycle calls remain separate obligations.
Creation failure is checked before a successful commit. Unknown commit acknowledgements and external database mutation are outside these projections.

Real Core conformance covers exclusive callback-free cancellation, original-deadline restoration and stop success/failure races. action read(q: Cursor): bool = {
    val eligible = s.rows.filter(id => q.after < id and id <= q.through)
    val first = eligible.fold(4, (smallest, id) => if (id < smallest) id else smallest)

      else if (q.after > q.through or q.through > s.sequence) "invalid"
      else if (first == s.blocked) "projection-error"
      else "ok"
    val complete = status == "ok" and eligible.size() <= 1
    val nextAfter = if (complete) q.through else first
    s' = { ...s,
      cursor: if (status == "ok") { ...q, after: nextAfter } else s.cursor,
      page: { query: q, status: status, complete: complete,
        returned: if (status == "ok" and eligible != Set()) Set(first) else Set() },
    }
  }

Real AgentRuntime and PGlite replay successful retry after false, refusal through exhaustion, and an observer rejection after confirmed commit using synthetic tier-0 input. They check the marker at completion, read/write attempt counts and a later deduplicated request.

bounds.external-query-retirement: One agent, two service identities, two adapter identities, two query slots and two registrations. One scheduler stop and restart plus adapter retirement. The adapter owner may be absent from queried services. Query success, failure and delayed results retain exact service and adapter ownership until settlement.
bounds.batch-registration-replacement: Two agents in one already-admitted query batch and one fresh query for the waiting peer task. One scheduler generation and a shared storage connection. The first service can remain in runTick while the peer registers its replacement and unregisters its old service. Results are grouped in storage order. Worker internals, query failures, empty periodic ticks and other generations are abstracted or checked in the adjacent models.

assumptions: No fairness assumption. A service unregisters synchronously before its outstanding query receipts are drained.
No fairness assumption. Exact service identity and retirement prevent a closed runtime from owning a new query.
Weak fairness of query settlement and closeStorage for each service. Every admitted adapter query eventually returns or throws, and the host waits for service stop before closing that runtime.
Weak fairness of query settlement and returnSchedulerStop. The stop receipt covers queries captured before the generation was detached, and later generations retain their own query owners.
Weak fairness of query settlement and closeAdapter for each adapter. Every admitted adapter query eventually returns or throws. A retired adapter is not reopened by the host.

Weak fairness of advance. The admitted query and first service settle, the scheduler continues to the next group, a pending replacement task gets a fresh query, and the peer work settles. The projection covers one queued one-shot task for each of two agents and one replacement registration.
No fairness. A held earlier service or a delayed scheduler continuation can leave the replacement task pending.

limitations: The finite query ownership case uses two service identities, two adapter identities and two query slots for one agent. TaskScheduler retains the dirty-agent and dispatch model.
The adapter owner may be absent from the queried service identities. Runtime.close fences and drains its exact adapter while preserving a different active adapter.
Per-service worker and preflight drainage are covered separately by TaskRetirement. A hung adapter call cannot satisfy the stated progress assumption.

Real PGlite conformance checks delayed queries, stale query failure, unregister and adapter-owner closure across two runtimes. Host reopening of retired adapters remains outside this model. Agent runtime-lifecycle models the host-confirmed physical alias handoff separately and binds real shared PGlite handle conformance. Core never inspects physical connections.

The batch projection checks two distinct agents on one PGlite connection, one scheduler generation, one replacement registration and one fresh query for the peer task after the first dispatch settles. Real conformance holds the first worker, replaces and unregisters the peer service, rejects stale dispatch, and reads both one-shot removals from the database. Larger batches and combined batch replacement with scheduler restart remain outside this projection.
